name: The Joker
fact: The Joker was the villain in Batman's very first issue (without the title of 'Detective Comics,') and was initially supposed to be killed off, but was saved by editorial intervention. This decision would allow him to become Batman's archenemy, and become the majority favourite among fans. In his earlier appearances, he was merely a comical prankster, then once the 'Comics Code Authority' lifted some of its rules, he became more of an evil character.

name: Bane
fact: Bane proved to be one of Batman's most physical threats when he broke his back in the comic book 'Knightfall,' causing Batman to rise back up both mentally and physically. Bane is also one of the most intelligent villains in the rogues gallery.

name: Ra's Al Ghul
fact: Ra's Al Ghul has been alive for hundreds of years due to bathing in the Lazarus Pit, giving him the supernatural ability to stay young. He is the leader of the League of Assassins and is the father of Talia Al Ghul, the mother of Batman's son, Damian Wayne.

name: Mr. Freeze
fact: Mr. Freeze, also known as Victor Fries, originally had the name Mr. Zero when he was created. He was a scientist who studied cryonics. His wife Nora had an incurable disease, and with his knowledge on cryonics, he found a way to freeze his wife while she was still alive, so he can do the necessary research to save her.

name: The Penguin
fact: The Penguin, also known as Oswald Cobblepot, was ranked #51 in IGN's list of 'Top 100 Comic Book Villains.' Cobblepot is Gotham City's most feared and powerful underground crime boss. With his influence in the city, his iconic purple umbrella, which is also a weapon, and his exploding wind-up penguins, he's a great threat to Batman, relying on more than brute strength.

name: The Riddler
fact: The Riddler, also known as Edward Nygma, or Edward Nashton, has one of the most brilliant minds. He knew he was smarter than anyone in any room he was in, and his ego grew to the point of obsession. His obsession with being the smartest person in the room was nothing compared to when Batman solved his deadly game of riddles, forever seeing Batman as his true rival.

name: The Scarecrow
fact: The Scarecrow, also known as Jonathan Crane, was a scientist who studied the psychology of fear and the effects of the mind. Crane developed a hallucinogen that made those who were exposed to it see their worst fears, and in the worst cases, either drive them insane or cause them to die of a heart attack. Batman has been the only one to successfully overcome Scarecrow's drug and stop his mission to cause fear around the city.

name: Harley Quinn
first-appearance: Batman: The Animated Series, Episode 22 ('Joker's Favor')
fact: Harley Quinn was not created for a comic book, unlike most other characters on this list, instead she was an original character for Batman's television show in the 90s. Harleen Quinzel was a therapist, working at the mental institute 'Arkham Asylum.' One of her infamous patients was The Joker. Quinzel was fascinated by him from the start, and grew an attachment to him. She became obsessed with The Joker and helped break him out of Arkham Asylum. She changed her name to 'Harley Quinn' and became his right-hand woman.

name: Killer Croc
fact: Killer Croc, also known as Waylon Jones, was a former sideshow wrestler. He had a rare genetic condition that gave him reptilian features and superhuman strength. This condition drove him mad and he turned to a life of crime. As he became older, he grew stronger and his appearance became more reptilian, fully committing himself to be the monster everyone sees.

name: Man-Bat
fact: Man-Bat is a mutation, accidentally created by the human inside. Dr. Robert Kirkland Langstrom was a zoologist who experimented with bat DNA. He wanted to give the human race the ability of acute sonar sense just like a bat. When he experimented on himself, he mutated into a giant bat and lost control of himself in this form. Man-Bat would terrorize the city, even killing his own wife in the chaos.

name: Two-Face
fact: Two-Face, also known as Harvey Dent, was a district attorney for Gotham City. He was loved by the citizens of the city and had the name 'The White Knight,' since he was seen as the savior of Gotham, finally taking down the criminal underworld and making the city great again. Unfortunately, when a hitman scarred half of his face with acid, he developed a multiple personality disorder from the trauma. Now he sees justice taken by chance, flipping a coin to decide the fate of his life and the life of others, even if it means death.

name: Poison Ivy
fact: Poison Ivy, also known as Pamela Lillian Isley, had a Ph.D. in botany, the study of plants. She experimented with a mix of chemicals from plants. Once she injected herself with them, she gained the ability to control plants at will and even speak with them. From then on, she became a voice for nature, and saw humans as a threat. Poison Ivy attempts to protect nature at all costs, even if it means all civilization must perish.

name: Catwoman
fact: Catwoman, also known as Selina Kyle, was a master thief who could slip in and out of high-security buildings to retrieve cash and jewels. Selina grew up homeless, without parents. She learned to fend for herself and didn't care about breaking the law. Catwoman and Batman, who were enemies of each other, would eventually grow into a flirtatious, yet complicated relationship. Catwoman would even help Batman with certain missions and be a part of the 'Bat-Family.'

name: Clayface
fact: Clayface, also known as Basil Karlo, was a film actor. When he hears they are filming a remake of a movie he starred in, he becomes desperate to stay relevant as an actor, and he gets into contact with Daggett Industries. They developed a serum that gives anyone the ability to control facial muscles at will, giving Basil the ability to 'out-act' any other actor. But when he gets into contact with the serum, his skin becomes clay-like. He can form his body into any shape, even impersonate other people. However, his mental state couldn't handle the process, and he turned to a life of crime.

name: Firefly
fact: Firefly, also known as Garfield Lynns, was a pyromaniac with an obsessive compulsion to start fires and commit arson. He would cause terror around the city. Eventually, he got caught in his own fire, and suffered third-degree burns all over his body. Lynns would survive, but this would not stop his crimes, instead would fuel his hatred and insanity. He would build a suit that would allow him to fly and commit more direct crimes.
